```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
#| label: read-data
files <- list.files("data", pattern = "^yob.*\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE)

baby_names <- read_csv(
  files,
  col_names = c("name", "sex", "n"),
  col_types = "cci",
  id = "file"
) |>
  mutate(year = parse_number(basename(file))) |>
  select(year, sex, name, n)
```

Using records from the US Social Security Administration from 1880 to 2025, we can observe how popular baby names rise and fall across different eras.

```{r}
#| label: plot-names
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
baby_names |>
  filter(name %in% c("Mary", "Linda", "Emma"), sex == "F") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n, color = name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(
    title = "Popularity of Selected Names Over Time",
    subtitle = "Annual counts for female babies in the United States (1880–2025)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of Babies",
    color = "Name",
    caption = "Source: US Social Security Administration"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```
